title: Three-Dimensional Shapes and Their Nets
seo_title: 3D Shapes and Nets – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, pyramids and prisms; count faces, edges and vertices; match solids to their nets. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on 3D shapes: cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, prisms and pyramids, faces, edges and vertices, and nets. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A net folds up to make a solid.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A face is a flat or curved surface, an edge is where two faces meet and a vertex is a corner.
  • A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A triangular prism has 5 faces.
  • A net is a flat shape that folds to make a solid. A cube has 11 different nets.

Examples

Example

Square-based pyramid

1 square + 4 triangles

Answer: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting hidden edges twiceCount each edge once.
Calling a cylinder a circleA circle is flat; a cylinder is solid.
Thinking every 6 squares make a cube netFold it in your mind and check that no faces overlap.

faq.q: What solid is a tin of tomato paste?

faq.a: A solid with the same cross-section all along its length.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is standing on a triangle face, but it is still a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a square-based pyramid.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.
It has 1 circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cone.
It is round all over, like a ball, so it is a sphere. A circle is a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: Both pictures show the same 3-D shape in different positions. What is it?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. Turning a shape does not change its name.
It has 2 circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. Turning a shape does not change its name.
C is a cone: it has 1 circle face and comes to a point. It is lying on its side.
D is a cuboid: it has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares. It is standing on its end.
B is a triangular prism: it has 2 triangle faces joined by rectangles. It is standing on a triangle.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: The two end faces are hexagons (6 sides) joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism. A hexagon is a 2-D shape.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: How many edges does a tetrahedron have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: I am a 3-D shape with 6 faces. All of my faces are squares of the same size. What am I?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces that are all equal squares. A cuboid has rectangular faces.

items.q: I have 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles. What am I?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at the top make a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 4 faces, and all of them are triangles?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. A square-based pyramid has a square face as well.

items.q: What shape are the faces of a cuboid?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces (some of them can be squares, which are special rectangles).

items.q: Which of these 3-D shapes has no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over: it has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices (corners).

items.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at the top. They fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. They fold into a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: C is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: A folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which net folds into a square-based pyramid?
items.e: D has 1 square and 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. The net with only 3 triangles leaves one side open; the others make a triangular prism and a tetrahedron.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: B has 3 rectangles and 2 triangles, one triangle at each end. One wrong net has only 2 rectangles, one has both triangles at the same end, and one is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face D?
items.e: Faces D and C are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: Fold the net: face D lands opposite face A. A face that touches A in the net (B, F) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: Faces A and E are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: How many faces does a net of a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles: 1 + 4 = 5 faces.

items.q: Kelechi folds a net of 6 rectangles into a cuboid. How many edges does the cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 12 edges (and 6 faces and 8 vertices). 6 is the number of faces.
